title: Capture Map
description: What the consultant's screen recording actually contains, scene by scene. Stage 1 output. Scene boundaries come from ffmpeg scene detection; the descriptive fields come from Claude reading the extracted keyframes. The split matters: 'in'/'out' are measured, 'screen'/'action'/'observed' are read, and read_status says which scenes have actually been looked at.

slug.description: Used in the run workspace directory name

system.description: The system being demonstrated, in the client's own naming, e.g. 'S/4HANA Fiori'

audience.description: Role the module is for, e.g. 'Requisitioners'

source.description: Measured by ffprobe. Never hand-written — if these are wrong every downstream timing is wrong.

path.description: Path to the recording, relative to the run workspace

detection.description: How the boundaries were found, recorded so a re-run with a different threshold is comparable.

threshold.description: ffmpeg select='gt(scene,N)' value. Raise it if the recording is split too finely, lower it if steps are being merged.

manual_overrides.description: Boundaries the practitioner added or removed by hand after reviewing the contact sheet

guide_transcript.description: Path to the consultant's spoken walkthrough as transcribed by Synthesia on upload. The SME source for Stage 2 narration. Absent means the module was recorded silent and narration has no SME backing beyond the frames.

scenes.description: Ordered, non-overlapping, and together covering the whole source duration. qa_video.py checks that tiling; gaps between scenes are a coverage failure, not a rounding detail.

in.description: Seconds from the start of the source

duration.description: out - in, stored so downstream scripts need not recompute

frame_ref.description: Extracted keyframe. Required unless disposition is 'cut'.

disposition.description: keep = narrate it. cut = drop it (dead air, mis-click, private data on screen). accelerate = keep but speed up, typically a loading spinner.

disposition_note.description: Required when disposition is 'cut' or 'accelerate'. Footage does not get dropped without a stated reason.

screen.description: What screen this is, in the system's own naming

action.description: What happens during the scene — the control acted on, the field filled

observed.description: Specific things visible in the frame that narration may safely refer to. Anything not listed here is not established by the frame.

read_status.description: 'read' means the keyframe was actually looked at and screen/action/observed reflect it. 'unread' means the scene is a boundary stub only. Writing narration against an 'unread' scene is what invariant 1 exists to prevent.
